description: fz-go4.18.12 finding 5 — the correctness-critical one (non-determinism doctrine). On fixtures2/00001_quicksort_plus_foo.fz, two identical runs differ in 21 (job kind, key) histogram entries: the activation arrow Ty ids THEMSELVES differ per schedule (Ty(64) vs Ty(65) for the same role) — program output identical, but activation keys are schedule-dependent. Also: append is demanded at TWO arrows (Ty(59), Ty(61)); Ty(59)'s RuntimeDemand is produced then never materialized — a widen-then-retract activation-keying arc leaving an orphaned demand. DIAGNOSE: why does the same role key to different interned arrows under different schedules (interning order leaking into key identity? provisional arrow minted pre-settlement? relates to fz-hwn.27 canonical addressed arrows + the fz-go4.18.3.2.1 canonicalization + fz-y6w convergence_class)? The orphaned provisional demand is the widen-then-retract shape the minimality doctrine flags. Related note: 00001 materializes fz_op_add_if x3 / fz_op_add_ff x2 in an ALL-INTEGER program — map-value erasure at stats[:k] widens + to any+any, materializing the whole overload web (fz-y6w/fz-3bb territory; may share the provisional-arrow root). Sequencing: findings 1-3 (trace churn) land first so this diagnosis reads a clean trace. ACCEPTANCE for the diagnosis: root cause named with evidence; 0 histogram diff keys across runs on 00001 after the fix (or a proven-benign classification of residual variance).

comments.text: Re-scoped context: schedule-dependent arrow keys are plausibly keys minted from MID-ASCENT demand values (the .18.22 founding defect). Post-.18.22 demand is deterministic (unique least fixpoint) — re-run the 2-run histogram diff on 00001 first; the orphaned provisional-arrow demand should also vanish. Diagnose only what survives.

Corroborating evidence from the fz-go4.18.22 rework (F2 root-cause): on fixtures2/behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2, the BackendProgram differs on every run of the same build — generated FunctionIds (161/162) swap between the two lambda executables and transport position orderings churn — and the interp answer flips {'10,10'|'2,2'} accordingly (both wrong; expected '10,2'; the two dbg callsites print one conflated closure result). Present identically on f92375bc6, 0810fcb89, and the F1-fixed rework; demand productions are 3/0-identical on all, so the non-determinism is in arrow/executable keying + backend assembly, not in RuntimeDemand.

title: Activation arrow keying is schedule-dependent on 00001; demanded executable at retracted arrow is orphaned
